Users could only turn off an automation with the DESTRUCTIVE /cancel|/forget, so they deleted configs they'd have kept through travel/noise. Added a non-destructive pause/resume: 'snooze btc 3 days' / 'pause my morning digest' / 'snooze all' / 'resume btc'. Every proactive thing (reminders, dailies, alerts, digests, recipes) is a Schedule record — reminders directly, alerts/digests/recipes as alert:/digest:/recipe: markers — so ONE pausedUntil flag on Schedule + a single runner skip covers all of them. New parseSnoozeCommand (duration grammar: min/hour/day/week; indefinite=PAUSE_INDEFINITE) + ScheduleStore.pause/resume/matchByRef/clearExpiredPause. matchByRef resolves an id, a marker name, or a task substring; 'all' hits every schedule. The runner skips a paused schedule WITHOUT firing or completing (so it resumes on its original schedule), and auto-clears an elapsed timed snooze; resume() pulls a stale recurring dueMs forward to now so it fires next tick without a backlog storm. Handler branch runs before the schedule cue so 'pause/snooze/resume' aren't misread as new reminders; help text + wiring added. 17 tests (parser / store pause+resume+expire / runner skip+auto-resume / handler routing). call-tested: false (offline unit; no live keys needed — pure scheduler logic). 1115 tests green.

Schedules/recipes/digests/alerts each had their own /list command, so a user with a few automations ran four commands to see what's running and lost track. Added /dashboard (+ /dash alias): one at-a-glance rollup — reminders with next-fire, watches with their trigger + last-seen value, digests with member count + cadence, recipes with run hint, and a ⏸ paused marker (with resume time) on anything snoozed. New pure src/lib/dashboard.ts formatDashboard (empty -> onboarding nudge, empty sections omitted, long tasks one-lined); index dashboardView gathers from the live stores, owning the tz offset (formatWhen) + reading pause state off each automation's scheduled marker row. Registered in setMyCommands + help + KNOWN_COMMANDS. 7 tests (formatter: empty/sections/paused/digest+recipe/truncation + handler routing /dashboard & /dash). call-tested: false (pure read of local stores, no live keys). 1122 tests green.

Fixed a confidently-wrong first-errand: get_weather used forecast_days=1 while the prompt told the agent to ALWAYS use it for any forecast question, so 'will it rain tomorrow?' returned TODAY's numbers. Bumped Open-Meteo to forecast_days=7 + daily weather_code; parseForecast now builds a days[] array (each day its own code/hi/lo/precip, today/current kept for back-compat). Added a 'when' tool param + resolveWhen (tomorrow/this weekend/named weekday/this week -> day indices, derives todayDow from days[0].date, no clock) + formatDay/formatWeatherWhen; the dispatch reports the requested future day(s), falling back to the current line for a today/now question. 8 tests + LIVE call-tested against Open-Meteo (7-day array w/ per-day codes + dates). 1130 tests green.

Fixed a regression from the just-shipped snooze feature: 'snooze all' / 'pause <x>' with no duration set PAUSE_INDEFINITE on EVERY matched schedule including one-shot reminders, so 'remind me at 3pm' set before a trip was frozen forever until a manual resume — a silent black hole for the highest-trust item. ScheduleStore.pause now skips kind==='once' when the pause is INDEFINITE (snooze is for quieting recurring noise; a discrete promise shouldn't freeze forever). A TIMED snooze of a once is still allowed — the runner's clearExpiredPause auto-resumes it when the window elapses, so it fires later, not never. 2 tests (indefinite pause-all leaves a once live + still pauses the recurring; timed snooze of a once is allowed). call-tested: false (pure scheduler logic). 1132 tests green.

Fixed a silent wrong-value miss on the headline threshold-alert feature: extractValue fell back to the LARGEST-magnitude number, so an 'S&P 500 below 6000' watch compared the Dow's 42,000 in a multi-index reply and never fired. Added an optional `hint` (the watched task) to extractValue/conditionHolds/changed, threaded from alert-runner (alert.task) at every call site. When >1 candidate survives the currency/decimal ordering AND the hint's entity words appear in the reply, it picks the number that comes closest AFTER an entity mention (financial phrasing is '<entity> <value>'), excludes numbers that are part of the entity's own name (the '500' in 'S&P 500'), and falls back to largest-magnitude with no/unmatched hint (existing behavior unchanged, all prior tests green). 3 tests (entity-nearest / no-hint regression / below-alert fires on the right index). call-tested: false (pure parse logic). 1135 tests green.

Closed the last two alert paths that flapped on a transient numberless reply (the threshold + predicate paths already guarded it). (1) PLAIN change-alert (no threshold): a reply that lost its number ('price temporarily unavailable') fell through to changed()'s text-diff, false-pinged '🔔 changed', and stored the garbage as baseline — now, if the last value tracked a number and the new one has none, skip notify + keep the last GOOD value. Non-numeric watches (top HN story) are unaffected: their baseline has no extractable number so the guard never triggers. (2) WATCHLIST members: same guard per-member — a member whose numeric baseline gets an 'N/A' this tick isn't flagged changed and its baseline isn't overwritten (used extractValue with the member's own task as hint). Also threaded the extractValue entity-hint into the watchlist changed() call. 3 tests (plain-change numberless silent+baseline-kept / non-numeric watch still fires / watchlist member numberless not-flagged+baseline-kept). call-tested: false (pure alert logic). 1138 tests green.

Fixed a silent no-op on common recurring cadences: the interval regex only matched min/hours and the relative regex only min/hours/days, so 'water the plants every 2 days', 'newsletter every other week', 'renew the lease in 3 weeks' all fell through parseSchedule (returned null) and ran ONCE as a browse — the user thought a recurring reminder was set and it never fired. Extended the interval regex to days/weeks + 'other' (=2 weeks/days) and the relative regex to weeks; the interval kind already advances by whole gaps on complete, so no runner change. Widened the handler scheduleCue so 'every N days/weeks' / 'in N weeks' reach the parser instead of the one-shot agent path. 4 tests (every 2 days / every 1 week + every other week / in 3 weeks / handler-cue reaches scheduleAdd). call-tested: false (pure parse + cue). 1142 tests green.

A digest member recipe that's a '>>' chain ran the literal 'step a >> step b' as ONE confused agent task — the /run + scheduled-recipe paths already run chains via runChain, but digest-runner called runAgent(rec.task) directly, so a chained member silently poisoned the briefing with off-topic prose presented as real data. Added a runChain dep + isChain guard to digest-runner mirroring schedule-runner: a chain member runs as a sequential workflow, its final output becomes that section (empty -> the '(couldn't fetch)' fallback), falling back to runAgent when runChain isn't wired. Wired runChain into index's digestRunText (used by both /run and scheduled digests). 3 tests (chain member -> runChain not literal / no-runChain falls back to runAgent / empty chain -> fallback line). call-tested: false (offline unit; chain needs live LLM for a true e2e). 1145 tests green.

Fixed a dead-watch bug: a watchlist member whose FIRST check errored (last stays undefined) and then recovered on a later tick where no other member changed was never seeded — the runner returned commit:noop on the all-unchanged tick, discarding its update, and the `mem.last !== undefined` change-guard then kept it out of changedLines forever, so it silently never alerted again. On a no-notify tick the runner now seeds any member still missing a baseline immediately (committing only the fresh seeds, no send to gate on); an already-seeded unchanged member is not re-written. 2 tests (missed-first-check member gets seeded on a quiet tick + unchanged member not re-committed / fully-unchanged all-seeded watchlist writes nothing). call-tested: false (pure alert logic). 1147 tests green.

Fixed a chain if-gate firing on the OPPOSITE condition: containsUnnegated only inspected the 12 chars before the keyword, so 'not currently in stock' ('not' 14 chars out) read as un-negated and an 'if in stock: buy/notify' chain ran on the inverse. Replaced the fixed window with a clause scan — from the nearest boundary (. ! ? ; : newline, or a ' but '/' and ' conjunction) up to the keyword — looking for any negation (not/no/never/without/out of/no longer/isn't/aren't/won't/can't/n't). So 'no longer available', 'never got it back in stock', "isn't currently in stock" all correctly fail the gate, while a negation in a DIFFERENT clause ('sold out online but in stock at the store') still passes. 2 tests (far-negation fails gate / different-clause negation still matches). call-tested: false (pure predicate logic). 1149 tests green.

Fixed a one-shot reminder silently becoming permanent spam: the weekly branch guard accepted any '\bat\b', so 'remind me Friday at 3pm to submit taxes' (a single weekday + time, no 'every') parsed kind:weekly and pinged every Friday forever — and there was no way to get a single next-weekday reminder. The weekly branch now recurs ONLY when the user signalled repetition ('every', a weekday/weekend group, or >1 named day); a lone weekday+time returns kind:once at the next occurrence (nextWeeklyMs already computes the right instant). 3 tests ('Friday at 3pm' -> once on a Friday / 'every friday' stays weekly / 'mon and thu' stays weekly). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1152 tests green.

A cold user's first 'weather'/'coffee near me' dead-ended on a typed city ask (hunt for 📎→Location or type + spell a city). The inbound location-pin path was already wired, so added a Telegram request_location reply-keyboard button: new telegram.ts sendLocationRequest (one-time, resize keyboard) + a requestLocation method on the Channel interface (telegram wires it; console omits it) + an optional requestLocation handler dep. The near-me/weather location-ask now sends the tap-to-share button (falls back to a plain sendMessage when the channel lacks it, e.g. console), and the tapped pin flows into the existing saveCoords path. The tz-ask branch stays plain text (a pin gives coords, not a tz offset). 2 handler tests (button used when wired / plain fallback when not). call-tested: false (reply_markup needs a live bot; offline unit covers routing). 1154 tests green.

A scheduled digest whose member recipes were ALL deleted (but the digest kept) fired a contentless '📋 name' — or a briefing of nothing but '(no such recipe anymore)' removal notices — on cadence: recurring noise from a dead automation. runDigest now returns null when NO member produced real content (0 members, or every section is a placeholder — deleted/slotted/failed), and the schedule-runner treats a null digest like a deleted recipe: complete (advance/drop) + no send. A digest with >=1 real section still sends normally (a transient '(couldn't fetch)' on one member doesn't blank it). The inbound /run path already shows 'empty or gone' on null, so it's consistent. Each section now carries a real/placeholder flag. 5 tests (all-deleted -> null / no-members -> null / >=1 real still sends / chain-empty-alongside-real / existing cases). call-tested: false (offline unit). 1157 tests green.

A multi-slot recipe filled positionally with a multi-word value silently mis-mapped: '/run track oat milk HEB' on 'track {item} at {store}' whitespace-split to item='oat', store='milk', dropped 'HEB' — a confident WRONG run on a saved automation with no signal. Added slotsAmbiguous(task,args): flags a 2+-slot recipe filled positionally (no name=value pairs, no comma) whose whitespace token count != slot count. index recipeResolve returns an {ambiguousArgs, slots} shape in that case (like the existing missingArg path); the handler asks for a clean form ('item=… store=…' or comma-separated) instead of running the mis-split task. A matching token count, comma form, or name=value pairs still fill unambiguously; a single-slot recipe still takes the whole arg. 10 tests (5 slotsAmbiguous unit: mismatch flagged / 2=2 + comma + pairs unambiguous / single-slot never / empty-args never; + handler asks-not-runs). call-tested: false (pure parse + routing). 1162 tests green.

Widened the greeting/capability onboarding match so a new user's ACTUAL first message gets the instant /start card instead of a 10-30s floundering browse. CAPABILITY_RE required what/who/how + can/do/are/is + you/this, missing 'what's this?', 'what does this do?', 'who are you', 'how do you work'. Rebuilt as anchored alternatives (what's/is this[ bot] / what does this do / what can/do you do / who are you / how do you work) with a small closing-filler tail + the existing <=6-word gate, so real tasks ('what does this error mean', 'how does this recipe work in the oven', 'who are you texting for the party') still fall through to the agent. 2 tests (7 opener phrasings greet / 3 real-task guards fall through). call-tested: false (pure regex + handleCommand). 1163 tests green.

The proactive half of Relay ran dumber than the reactive half: the inbound path threads nowMs/tzOffsetMin/weatherCoords/weatherUnits into runAgent, but every proactive caller (schedule/alert/digest/chain runner) called runAgent(task,{llm,context},[]) with none — so a scheduled 'top news today'/'days until my trip' reasoned from the model's training date and a metric user's daily weather came back in °F. Added an AgentEnv type + an optional agentEnv(chatId) dep to all four runners (widening their runAgent dep to carry the fields), spread into every proactive runAgent call. index wires a shared agentEnvFor(chatId) = {nowMs: Date.now(), tzOffsetMin from profile, weatherCoords freshCoords, weatherUnits from profile} into the schedule runner, alertCheck, digestRunText (+ its runChain), the trigger-to-action runThen, scheduled runChain, and the inbound runChainRecipe. So proactive runs now get the same buildNowLine + unit-aware get_weather the inbound path does. 1 test (schedule tick threads nowMs/tz/units into runAgent). call-tested: false (offline unit proves the deps thread through). 1164 tests green.

The anti-spam send-cap dropped alert CHECKS, not just sends: an over-cap recurring schedule was safeComplete'd + advanced, so for an 'alert:'-marked schedule the whole check was skipped and a 'below 50k' crossing during a capped hour was never evaluated and never re-fired (a below->above->below bounce lost). The headline watch feature silently missed the exact event it promised. Fixed: an alert: marker now bypasses the send-cap gate and falls through to fireOne — alertCheck is edge-triggered (sends ONLY on a real change) so it self-throttles and can't storm; a resulting send still calls noteSend so cap accounting stays honest, and the baseline commit still gates on a successful send. Dailies/reminders stay capped. 2 tests (over-cap alert still checks + sends its crossing / over-cap unchanged alert checks but stays silent). call-tested: false (offline unit). 1166 tests green.

Made snooze/pause surgical: matchByRef used label.includes(w) with no tiering, so 'pause news' could also freeze a reminder that merely mentioned 'news' — the user silences the wrong automation. Now tiered: an exact id/label wins outright; else a whole-word (\bword\b) match ('news' hits 'news'/'morning news', not 'call about the news story'); only if nothing matches on a word boundary does it fall back to a raw substring (keeping the btc->btcusd convenience). Regex-escaped the term. 3 tests (word-boundary beats unrelated substring / exact label beats longer label / substring fallback when no word hit). call-tested: false (pure store logic). 1169 tests green. NOTE: backlog was dry except owner-gated confirm-to-act, so instead of a fresh 3-agent audit (would duplicate audit 24's still-unbuilt findings) I refilled from audit 24's deferred set — seeded snooze-zero-duration-guard(S), background-errand-progress-ping(S), package-tracking-watcher(M).

A detached 'get back to me' errand ACKed 'on it' then ran for minutes with NO progress signal — the LONGEST tasks (most likely to look hung) were the only ones with zero mid-run reassurance, so a first-timer assumes it died. Armed the same one-shot progress timer the sync agent + chain paths use in dispatchBackground: after progressDelayMs, send one 'Still on it — I'll text you the moment it's done', cleared as soon as the errand settles (success OR error path). Reuses the handler's setTimer/clearTimer deps; disabled when progressDelayMs is absent (console channel). 1 test (a background run outlasting the delay sends the interim ping + the final result still lands). call-tested: false (offline unit). 1170 tests green.

Added a track_package agent tool so 'where's my package 1Z999...' / 'track 9400...' resolves the carrier + reads the right tracking page instead of a logged-out flounder. New src/lib/tracking.ts: detectCarrier(number) by shape (UPS 1Z+16 / USPS 9x IMpb + SNN..US intl / FedEx 12-15-20 digit / DHL 10-digit + JJD), trackingUrl(carrier,number) -> the OFFICIAL public page, carrierName, parseTrackingRequest (pull the number from free text; an explicitly named carrier overrides shape). The dispatch drives anvil scrape on the built URL (a keyless GET 403s but real Chrome renders the status), truncateForModel's the page, and asks the model to summarize the latest status + ETA; unknown shape -> asks which carrier (never guesses). Wired into the tool surface + SYSTEM_PROMPT + help ('add "watch" to get pinged on a status change' — reuses the existing change-alert). 14 tests (detect x5 shapes / URL build / carrierName / parseTrackingRequest x3 / 2 agent dispatch: UPS scrape + unknown-carrier ask). call-tested: false (detection/URL pure-unit; the scrape needs live anvil, which is down). 1182 tests green.

Fixed a fat-finger black hole: 'snooze btc for 0 hours' / 'pause btc 0 days' — the duration regex matched but the old n>=1 guard left untilMs undefined AND didn't strip the clause, so the name became 'btc 0 hours' (no match) or fell through to an indefinite PAUSE_INDEFINITE, silently freezing btc forever. parseSnoozeCommand now ALWAYS strips the duration clause off the name and REJECTS a zero/negative duration (returns null) so it's a no-op, not an indefinite pause — the caller's non-snooze fall-through handles it; a positive duration on the same phrasing still parses. 1 test (0 hours + 0 days -> null / positive still parses). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1183 tests green.

Fixed a regression in the just-shipped track_package: it fed truncateForModel(r.content) to the model with only a !body.trim() empty check, skipping the formatPageForModel empty/paywall/JS-shell guard that scrape + read use. Carrier pages are heavily JS-rendered, so the common failure (a shell/cookie-wall stub) got summarized as an invented status instead of an honest 'couldn't read it'. Now uses formatPageForModel (near-empty <200 nonWs -> honest marker, paywall detection, truncation) + tells the model to relay 'couldn't read the page' when it sees the marker. 2 tests updated/added (real page summarizes + isn't flagged / JS-shell page returns the honest marker, not invented events). call-tested: false (offline unit; scrape needs live anvil). 1184 tests green.

Re-defining an alert via 'watch btc: bitcoin below 45000' on an EXISTING btc alert kept the stale lastValue — the define-overwrite path (AlertStore.add) only cleared the baseline on a feed toggle, unlike the conversational-edit path (updateTrigger) which clears it. So prevHolds computed from the old value and an already-true predicate was suppressed: the alert the user just set up was silently dead. add() now detects a real trigger change (task, threshold, or condition — deep-compared) and clears lastValue so the new trigger edge-evaluates fresh; a no-op re-define (identical trigger) PRESERVES the baseline so cumulative sub-threshold drift isn't lost. 2 tests (redefine-to-predicate clears baseline / identical redefine keeps it). call-tested: false (pure store). 1186 tests green.

Fixed a regression in the single-weekday-once rule: 'remind me mondays at 9am' scheduled ONCE then never again — the recurring test was every|group|weekdays.length>1, and a plural 'mondays' still resolves to one day [1] with no 'every', so the clear plural-'s' repetition signal was swallowed. The weekly branch now also treats a plural weekday token (mondays/fridays/tuesdays...) as recurring. The SINGULAR one-shot ('monday at 9am' -> once) is unaffected. 3 tests (mondays/fridays -> weekly / singular monday still once). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1188 tests green.

A tracking number pasted the way carriers PRINT it ('9400 1118 9922 3817 6123 45', '1Z 999 AA1 ...', '1234-5678-9012') failed to parse — parseTrackingRequest tokenized the raw text on \b[0-9A-Z]{10,}\b before norm() stripped separators, so a spaced number split into sub-10-char fragments matching nothing -> 'couldn't tell which carrier', despite the module's premise being 'users paste them'. Now also matches a spaced/dashed run of alnum GROUPS (each group required to contain a digit, so a leading 'TRACK'/'PACKAGE' word isn't swallowed), collapses the separators, and detects on the joined form; the single-run + 1Z patterns still catch no-space forms. 3 tests (spaced USPS + spaced UPS + dashed FedEx all resolve). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1189 tests green.

Closed the last recipe-execution path that ran a chain/slot recipe literally: an alert's 'then run <recipe>' (index runThen) called runAgent(rec.task) directly — no isChain/runChain, no hasSlots — so a 'then' recipe that was a '>>' chain or had a {slot} appended garbage (literal 'a >> b' / unfilled '{slot}') to the ping, degrading the watch-and-DO feature. runThen now skips a slotted recipe (no per-fire value) and runs a chain via runChain like /run + schedule + digest do, else the single runAgent. tsc-verified; relies on the existing trigger-to-action dep-contract tests + the digest-runner chain tests (same runChain integration) — the guard is a direct mirror of the tested digest-member path, and index's inline runThen isn't separately unit-harnessed. call-tested: false. 1189 tests green.

A 'coffee near me' / 'directions to X' answer was a dead end on a phone — name + straight-line distance, no way to navigate. Added lat/lng to the Place model (parsePlaces now carries the node coords) + a mapsLink helper (coords -> a pinned https://google.com/maps/search query, else a name search); formatPlaces appends a tappable link per row. Directions: added from/to coords to Route + a directionsLink helper (https://google.com/maps/dir with origin/destination coords or labels + travelmode from the mode); formatRoute appends it. So both marquee location errands are now tap-to-navigate. 4 tests (place link w/ coords + name-search fallback / route link w/ labels + coords). call-tested: false (pure format; live path needs anvil+Nominatim). 1191 tests green.

A standing 'weather near me every morning' set by a user who only shared a location PIN (no typed home city) silently died the same day: agentEnvFor (the proactive env) used profiles.freshCoords, which returns undefined past the 6h COORDS_TTL_MS, so the scheduled get_weather hit its 'no place, no location' branch and fired 'which city?' into the void forever. Added profiles.homeCoords (durable, TTL-ignoring) + switched agentEnvFor to it — a standing automation the user opted into keeps its location anchor, while the ad-hoc INBOUND path still uses freshCoords so the privacy TTL (don't leak a ~1m pin to the LLM on every later message) is unchanged. 1 profile test (homeCoords ignores TTL / undefined w/ no coords) + the existing freshCoords-expiry test still green. call-tested: false (pure store + wiring). 1192 tests green.

Everyday 'I'm in trouble' / 'I'm in bed' / 'I'm in the office' / 'I'm in a mood' was saved as the home location AND the message was eaten (never reached the agent) — parseSetLocation's bare-form guard only rejected task/scheduling keywords + >5-word tails, so a short state-of-being noun passed, corrupting the profile + losing the user's real message. Added two rejects to the bare 'I'm in X' form: a leading article (a/an/the — a real place-name has none) and a NON_PLACE state-of-being word list (trouble/bed/love/class/court/traffic/hospital/...). A proper-noun place with no article ('I'm in Paris', 'I'm in San Diego') still saves; the explicit /setlocation form stays permissive for any odd case. 1 test (6 non-place forms fall through / 2 real places still save). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1193 tests green.

Fixed a critical wrong-hour reminder: the daily/weekly time clause was only parsed when it sat right after the cadence word, so 'remind me every day to take my meds at 8pm' silently scheduled 9:00am (the default) AND left 'at 8pm' in the task — an evening reminder arriving 11h early every day. Added extractLooseAtTime(lower): finds the LAST 'at HH[:MM][am/pm]' anywhere in the message (am/pm or a colon-minute required, matching the main branches' discipline so 'look at 5 tabs' doesn't match). The daily + weekly branches use it as a fallback when no time sat adjacent, and strip the clause from the task; the morning/evening/night word-defaults still apply when there's no time anywhere. 2 tests (time-after-task on daily + weekly captured & stripped / word-default preserved). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1195 tests green.

Fixed a same-named-city timezone bug: inferTzFromLocation looped comma-parts leftmost-first, so 'Paris, TX' matched the CITY token (paris->UTC+1) before the disambiguating REGION token (tx->UTC-6) and fired every daily reminder ~7h off (also Dublin OH, Athens GA, Portland ME). Now a 'City, Region' form resolves the TAIL first (region wins), falling back to the leftmost city token only when the tail isn't a known region — so 'Paris, TX'->-360, 'Dublin, OH'->-300, 'Portland, ME'->-300, while 'Paris, France'->60 + 'Dublin, Ireland'->0 still resolve. Also filled in the missing US state abbrevs (ME/NH/VT/CT/RI/MD/WV/KY/WI/IA/KS/AR/AL/MS/ND/SD/MT/WY/AK) while OMITTING ones that collide with a city code or common English word (in/or/hi/la=Los Angeles/de/ok/id/ne) so a bare 'LA' still means Los Angeles. 3 tests (region disambiguation / foreign cities intact / LA no-collision). call-tested: false (pure inference). 1197 tests green.

The persistent answer-log (100 timestamped task+reply pairs/chat) had a search() but was write-only to the agent — only a whole-message isAnswerRecall regex in the handler could surface it, so a recall reference buried mid-request ('book me a table at that sushi place you found') never reached the log. Added a first-class recall(query) agent tool: a `recall` dep on AgentDeps (bound to the chatId by the handler via the existing recallAnswers/recallKeywords path), a tool def + dispatch that returns the top past answers with a relativeAge ('1h ago') so a stale price/story reads as past, and a graceful no-match ('offer to look it up fresh'). Wired into both the inbound + background runIt calls; the handler's whole-message recall fast-path stays. 4 tests (recall pulls past answer + shows age / no-match graceful + tool-surface pin). call-tested: false (offline unit; the LLM chooses to call it live). 1199 tests green.

detectCarrier mapped any bare 10-digit number to DHL (/^\d{10}$/), so 'track my order 1234567890' (a merchant ref / 10-digit phone) drove the agent to a DHL page + reported 'no DHL match' — implying the shipment didn't exist rather than that it wasn't a carrier number, contradicting the module's stated conservative-null contract. Dropped the bare-10-digit rule (kept JJD-prefixed DHL); a lone 10-digit now returns null so track_package asks which carrier, and it's still accepted as DHL when the user NAMES dhl (parseTrackingRequest's explicit-carrier branch, /^[0-9A-Z]{8,}$/). 3 tests (bare 10 -> null / JJD still DHL / named-dhl+10 tracks, bare order falls through). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1200 tests green.

Fixed the weakest path on the MOST-promoted first errand: crypto price ('save btc: check the price of bitcoin' is the literal /start + README example) had no tool — get_quote was equities-only + rejected 'bitcoin', so 'price of bitcoin' fell to a slow, flaky web_search+scrape and the flagship demo looked broken. New src/lib/crypto.ts hits the keyless CoinGecko API: a common-coin map (btc/eth/sol/doge/... -> id, skipping a round-trip) else the /search endpoint (top market-cap hit, so 'btc' -> Bitcoin not a clone), then simple/price for usd + 24h change; formatCrypto shows '▲/▼ +N% 24h' + extra precision for sub-$1 coins. Added a get_crypto agent tool + backend method + defaultBackend wiring + SYSTEM_PROMPT + help ('crypto + stock prices ... instantly'). 16 tests (crypto unit: common/search/parse/format/getQuote + 2 agent dispatch). LIVE call-tested: btc/eth (common, no search) + pepe (search->id) all resolved w/ price + 24h change. 1214 tests green.

Fixed a plain-English gap that bounced natural reminders: 'in an hour' / 'in half an hour' / 'in a couple hours' / 'in a few minutes' had no digit so the 'in \d+' relative match missed them (re-asked 'when?'), and 'set an alarm for 7am' / 'wake me at 6' (bare hour, no am/pm — the generic 'at' branch rejects it) never scheduled. parseSchedule now: (a) normalizes worded quantities to a digit (a/an/one=1, couple/two=2, few/several/three=3, half-an-hour=30min) before the relative match, stripping the ORIGINAL worded clause from the task (not the normalized one); (b) has an alarm branch parsing 'set an alarm for <time>' / 'wake me (up) (at) <time>' incl. a bare hour into a reminderOnly 'wake up' once at the next occurrence. Widened the handler scheduleCue to cue both. 2 tests (worded durations resolve + strip / alarm phrasing incl. bare hour). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1216 tests green.

Added calendar-date reminders — 'remind me on March 5', 'on the 15th', 'on Dec 25', 'next Monday' — appointment/birthday errands that previously bounced (parseSchedule only did relative/daily/weekly/interval + tomorrow/at-time). New branch before the weekly one: 'next <weekday>' -> that weekday's next occurrence (strips 'next' so it doesn't linger in the task — also fixes 'next friday at 3pm' which left 'next' in the task); 'on <Month> <day>' -> dateAtMs (this year, rolls to next year if past); 'on the <Nth>' -> domAtMs (this month if upcoming else next, month-by-month rollover for a 31st). A stated 'at <time>' sets the hour (else 9am default) via extractLooseAtTime; tz-aware. A month name with no day ('the march report') is NOT hijacked. Widened the handler scheduleCue. 5 tests (next-weekday / March 5 rolls to next year / Dec 25 this year + the 15th this month / at-time on a date / no-hijack). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1221 tests green.

A watchlist alert's 'then run <recipe>' was accepted by the parser but silently never ran — parseAlertCommand's semicolon/watchlist branch returned {name,task,members} without carrying `then`, and checkAlert's watchlist notify built its message without withThen. Fixed both: the watchlist branch now returns `then` (the then-clause was already stripped before the semicolon split, so members stay clean), and withThen was hoisted above the watchlist branch so a member-change ping runs the recipe + appends '▶ <recipe>: <output>' like the single-alert path. 2 tests (parse carries then through watchlist / checkAlert runs the then-recipe on a member change + appends output). call-tested: false (pure parse + alert logic). 1223 tests green.

Bundle-fixed 4 regressions the audit found in the just-shipped absolute-date + alarm branches: (1) the month regex had no word boundary after the 3-letter stem, so 'mark 5 emails'/'separate 3 files'/'junk 4 tabs'/'may 6 people' were hijacked into date reminders -> now a full month name OR a bounded 3-letter abbrev, and bare 'may N' only after 'on'; (2) 'next month' matched 'next mon'+th -> next Monday (~3 weeks early) -> next-weekday now matches full weekday words only; (3) 'set an alarm for 20 minutes' read 20 as an 8pm clock hour -> negative-lookahead skips a following min/hour/sec unit (it's a timer, falls through); (4) an alarm returned 'wake up' unconditionally, dropping the purpose -> cleanTask keeps 'to leave for the airport', bare alarm still 'wake up'. Mirrored the tightened patterns in the handler scheduleCue. 4 tests (prefix-collision / next-month / alarm-for-N-min / alarm-keeps-task). call-tested: false (pure parse). 1227 tests green.

Added a random/decision tool so a classic first-errand opener ('flip a coin', 'roll a d20', 'random number 1-100', 'pick one: tacos or sushi') gets a sub-second genuinely-random answer instead of a slow browse or an LLM-faked value. New src/lib/random.ts: parseRandomRequest (coin/dice 'NdM'/number-range/'up to'/'pick between/or/and' — anchored so 'a coin costs a dollar' isn't hijacked) + runRandom (RNG injected for deterministic tests). A `random` agent tool runs Math.random app-side + instructs the model to relay the EXACT result, never invent/re-roll. Wired into tool surface + SYSTEM_PROMPT + help. 17 tests (parse coin/dice/number/pick/no-hijack + splitOptions + seeded runRandom + 2 agent dispatch). call-tested: false (Math.random is app-side, deterministic under a seed in tests). 1240 tests green.

A pasted email/paragraph + 'make this shorter'/'proofread'/'tl;dr'/'rewrite this'/'translate this' was nudged by the tool-oriented SYSTEM_PROMPT toward web_search/scrape — a zero-latency errand turned slow/confused. Added a prompt carve-out to the ANSWER-DIRECTLY section: when the message CONTAINS the text to work on, process it with NO tool; never web_search/scrape for in-message text. Prompt-only (the live LLM chooses the behavior). Guarded via a SYSTEM_PROMPT-content test (pasted-text phrasing + 'never web_search or scrape for text' present) alongside the existing prompt-sync suite. 1 test. call-tested: false (prompt-only). 1241 tests green.

Named lists shipped: new src/lib/lists.ts (parseListCommand add/remove/show/clear + ListStore, atomic per-chat+name, caps 20 lists/100 items, case-insensitive dedupe + substring remove). Wired handler.listCommand branch before scheduler/agent, index.ts store + rendered replies (reads full list back on every mutation), RELAY_LISTS_FILE state path, .env.example + HELP text. Facts (remember X) confirmed already covered by notes.ts — this fills the NAMED-LIST gap. 22 new tests, full suite 1259 green, tsc clean.

Fixed list remove() collateral deletion: swapped raw substring (x.includes(q)) for notes.ts-style whole-word tiered scoring (3=exact wins alone, 2=all-words, 1=some-words). "remove milk" now removes only "milk", not "almond milk"/"milk chocolate". 3 new tests, suite 1261 green, tsc clean.

Added define tool: new src/lib/dictionary.ts (defineUrl/parseDefinition/formatDefinition/lookupWord) hitting keyless dictionaryapi.dev, mirroring get_crypto. Wired agent.ts (TOOLS entry, backend.defineWord + defaultBackend, dispatch block, prompt line), agent-dispatch pinned tool list, HELP text. "what does obsequious mean"/"define X"/"synonyms for X" now instant + sourced instead of model-memory or slow scrape. 10 new tests, suite 1271 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (dictionaryapi.dev origin returning 522 at build time — parser returns null on the HTML body -> graceful web_search fallback, verified offline against real response shape).

Added get_time tool: new src/lib/worldclock.ts (resolveZone via profile CITY_TZ + a tz-abbrev map PST/EST/JST/etc + UTC±offset parsing, parseClockTime, parseWorldClock now/convert, runWorldClock from injected nowMs). Wired agent.ts (TOOLS, dispatch using deps.nowMs, prompt), pinned tool list, HELP. "what time is it in Tokyo"/"9am PT in London"/"convert 3pm EST to Tokyo" now deterministic + instant instead of LLM guessing (datetime injection only covered the user own zone). Day-shift + standard-time (non-DST) caveat surfaced honestly. 15 new tests, suite 1286 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (pure offset math, no network).

Textual documents (CSV/JSON/TXT/MD/log) now read via the TEXT model instead of the vision path. describeDocument split by type (new src/lib/docs.ts isTextualDoc/decodeTextDoc/buildDocPrompt): textual -> decode bytes + complete(); pdf/image -> keep describeImage. A CSV was previously mislabeled image/jpeg (not in the MIME map) and fed to vision -> garbage. Threaded file_name + mime through telegram->handler->index. Now works even on a text-only provider. Added csv/tsv/json/md/xml/yaml to the download MIME map. 12 new tests + a handler routing test, suite 1295 green.

Backported mcp-forge DEV-0211: relay url-validator DoH rebind guard now FAILS CLOSED (both A+AAAA lookups failing -> treat host as blocked) instead of fail-open. Fixes a real SSRF hole (attacker forces DoH timeout to reach metadata IP) + restores shared-lib-parity (was red). Updated host-resolves tests to assert fail-closed + a clean-empty-still-allowed case. mcp-forge untouched (relay copy only).

atomicWriteJson now RETURNS a success bool + reports failures to a persist-error sink (setPersistErrorHandler, defaults to stderr) instead of silently swallowing. Threaded through NotesStore.add + ListStore.add (new saved flag). rememberFact + list-add confirmations now HEDGE honestly on a failed write (couldn't save to disk, may be lost on restart) instead of falsely confirming. 5 new tests. Suite 1298 green, tsc clean.

Completed the atomic-write-failure fix across all stores. persist() now returns bool + records lastWriteOk in Schedule/Alert/Recipe/Digest/Profile stores (getter lastSaveOk()). Confirmations for reminders (scheduleAdd), watches (alertDefine, both alert row + cadence schedule), recipe save (recipeSave + recipeSaveNamed), and digest define now HEDGE honestly (couldn't save to disk, may be lost on restart; alert also skips the run-now check) instead of falsely confirming. 3 new tests. Suite 1301 green, tsc clean.

Units now inferred from the resolved place country instead of defaulting the world to imperial. New src/lib/units.ts (inferUnitsFromPlace + resolveUnits): user pref wins; else infer (US/Liberia/Myanmar -> imperial, any other recognizable country tail -> metric); else keep imperial fallback (no regression for US-no-location). Clock-time 'once' reminders now tz-restamp on /setlocation. Added a clockTime flag set on every wall-clock once branch (at HH:MM, am/pm, alarm, next-weekday, on Month-day, on the Nth) + carried through Store.add. restampTz now shifts a FUTURE clock-time once's dueMs by the offset delta (UTC moves -Δ so wall-clock hour + calendar day hold) and updates its offsetMin; relative onces (no flag) and past-due onces are left alone. runDigest now distinguishes a transient all-fail from a structurally-dead digest. Replaced the boolean `real` per-section flag with a 3-way status: real | gone (deleted/slotted-skip, permanent) | failed (couldn't-fetch/degraded, transient). When no member is real: if any member FAILED -> return a '📋 name: couldn't put your briefing together this time (temporary blip), will try again' note so a relied-upon briefing never silently no-shows; only when ALL members are GONE -> return null (stay silent / 'empty or gone'), preserving empty-digest-fires-noise. 3 new tests (all-fail, all-degraded, mixed gone+failed). Suite 1342 green, tsc clean.

Feed items now dedup on a STABLE id (link/guid/objectID) not just the title. parseFeed returns FeedItem[] {title,id?}: RSS/Atom via new parseXmlItems (guid/id element or link href), Reddit .json (name/permalink), HN Algolia (objectID). alert-runner feedSource path keys on id:<id> when present, else t:<normTitle>, so a recurring 'Daily Discussion Thread' or two same-titled posts no longer collapse to one seen key and get dropped forever. parseXmlTitles kept as a titles-only back-compat wrapper. fetchFeed dep + wiring updated to FeedItem[]. 6 new/updated tests (id parsing, same-title-distinct-id fires). Added a contacts book so compose drafts to a saved recipient. complete() now returns the persist bool + guards a once against double-firing on a failed disk write. A once is marked delivered=true BEFORE the removal write; dueNow() excludes delivered items so it can't re-fire this session even if the splice-write failed; the item is spliced from memory only on a successful persist (a later persist drops it). schedule-runner logs a complete_persist_failed warn when complete() returns false. Was: complete() spliced the once then discarded persist()'s result, so on a full/unwritable disk the once vanished in memory but survived on disk -> duplicate ping after restart. 3 new tests. Suite 1380 green, tsc clean.

Bounded each proactive fire with a per-task wall-clock timeout (RELAY_FIRE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 90s, 0 disables). tick() runs due tasks sequentially with only step caps + per-fetch timeouts (no overall bound), so one hung anvil/LLM run blocked every other chat's due reminder. withFireTimeout races fireOne against the ceiling; a timeout rejects into the existing per-task catch (a once retries next tick, a recurring advances), so the batch moves on. Injectable timers (setTimer/clearTimer deps) for tests; real timers unref'd otherwise. 1 new test (hung task times out, 2nd chat still fires). .env.example documented. Suite 1381 green, tsc clean.

A corrupt store file that loads empty (data backed up to .corrupt) no longer wipes a user's reminders/alerts/recipes silently. Added a corruption sink to safe-store (setCorruptHandler, mirrors the persist-error sink); readJsonSafe reports each corruption + backup path. index installs the handler BEFORE constructing stores, collects human labels (reminders/watches/recipes/...), and exposes a corruptNotice() dep that drains once. Handler sends a one-time heads-up before handling the first inbound message. 4 new tests (sink fires on corrupt, not on missing/valid; handler notice once-only + silent-when-clean). Suite 1385 green, tsc clean.

Fixed the per-fire timeout (shipped last run) to CANCEL, not just abandon. withFireTimeout now threads an isCancelled flag into fireOne + flips it on timeout; fireOne checks it before the main send and before each early complete() (alert-silent, digest-null), so a slow run that finishes AFTER its ceiling is dropped instead of sending a duplicate/late ping + double-advancing the schedule (which also produced false 'watch failing' receipts). 1 new test (slow task finishing post-timeout sends nothing + doesn't re-advance). Suite 1386 green, tsc clean.

Hardened ContactStore.get so a fuzzy match can't draft to the wrong person. Now a contact matches ONLY when EVERY word of its name is present in the query, and only a UNIQUE match returns (most-specific by word-count when several are all-present; a genuine tie -> null so the caller asks which). 'text mom' no longer selects 'mom doctor'; 'email the big boss' still uniquely picks 'big boss'. 3 new tests. Suite 1389 green, tsc clean.

Added get_news tool: new src/lib/news.ts (newsUrl/parseHeadlines/formatNews/getNews) over the keyless Google News RSS feed (general top stories, or a topic search), reusing feeds.ts parseXmlItems + stripping the ' - Publisher' tail + deduping. Fixed inferTzFromLocation: a 'City, Region' whose region tail is a spelled-out place we don't know + isn't US no longer falls back to the leftmost US-city token. atomicWriteJson now fsyncs the temp file's contents before the rename (openSync/writeSync/fsyncSync/closeSync -> renameSync), so a hard crash/power-loss can't persist the rename while the bytes are still in the page cache (which produced the torn/empty file that trips the corrupt path + wipes a store). The module header claimed 'temp + fsync + rename' but there was no fsync — now true. Still never-throws + returns the success bool. 1 new test (durable overwrite, no torn state). Suite 1404 green, tsc clean.

Fixed future-day weather silently showing today. resolveWhen: 'next <weekday>' now resolves to the following week (+7, no today collision), and returns the day index even when it's past the forecast window. formatWeatherWhen: a beyond-window day returns an honest 'that day is beyond my N-day forecast' note (+ a partial note when only some requested days are out of range) instead of null -> which had made the agent render TODAY's numbers for a future question, the exact opposite of what the tool advertises. 3 new tests. Suite 1406 green, tsc clean.

Dropped cross-sport ambiguous team names (giants, rangers) from scores TEAM_LEAGUE. Was: 'did the Giants win' always answered SF Giants (MLB, never NY NFL); 'Rangers' always NHL (never Texas Rangers MLB / Rangers FC) — a confident wrong-sport answer, no hedge. A due digest over the hourly send-cap is no longer silently dropped for the day. Was: only once-reminders (grace-defer) + alert-checks were cap-exempt; a digest: (daily kind) hit safeComplete+continue -> advanced to tomorrow -> the relied-upon morning briefing just no-showed with an operator log. Now a digest gets the same defer-then-force grace as a once (leave it due, retry when a slot frees; force past the grace window rather than lose it). A plain daily/weather still drops its occurrence (re-fires on its own cadence, not a user-assembled bundle). 2 new tests (digest deferred+delivered later; plain daily still drops). Suite 1409 green, tsc clean.

The inbound sync turn wrote memory as [...history,...] using the pre-run snapshot read minutes earlier; a detached background errand (runs off the chain, the ack invites more texts) completing mid-turn had its result erased -> a follow-up had no memory of the errand. Now re-reads current memory at write time (memoryGet -> append -> memorySet, race-free with no await between), mirroring the errand-completion path's own re-read fix. 1 new regression test (interim errand write survives the sync turn). Suite 1410 green, tsc clean.

Added chart-a-watch: 'chart btc'/'graph my btc watch this week' renders the watch's recorded numeric series (watch-time-series) as a PNG line chart via keyless quickchart.io, sent through the existing sendPhoto path. New src/lib/chart.ts (parseChartRequest requiring an explicit chart/graph/plot word so a bare 'btc trend' still routes to the text watchTrend; chartUrl builds a Chart.js config URL; renderChart fetches + validates the PNG signature). Fixed scheduled-digest 'more'/'link' drilldown. recordSend cached the TRIMMED sent text as `full` (with sent=full.length), so 'more' said 'nothing more to show' + 'link' lost URLs on cut lines. recordSend dep now takes (chatId, full, sentLen); the scheduled path caches the UNTRIMMED composed digest + the trimmed send length (mirrors the inbound /run path). index recordSend updated. 1 new test (untrimmed digest cached, sent<full so a tail is pageable). Suite 1441 green, tsc clean.

Fixed agent-driven feed watch false-firing on prose. extractListItems kept ANY non-blank line as a feed item, so a one-line prose reply became an 'item' the agent reworded each check -> false '1 new' every time. Now: explicit bullet/ordinal markers -> take only those; no markers -> accept a bare list only when >=2 short non-sentence lines; otherwise (prose / single line) -> [] so the feed path finds nothing new + stays silent. The keyless feedSource path (stable ids) was already safe. 2 new tests (prose->[], bare multi-line list still counts). Suite 1443 green, tsc clean.

Fixed the handler error path clobbering memory. The catch wrote [...history,...] from the pre-run snapshot (read before the agent ran), so a background errand that delivered its result to memory mid-run had it erased when the run then threw — the same race the SUCCESS path was fixed for last runs, still live in the catch. Now re-reads current memory (memoryGet) + appends the failure note. 1 new regression test (errand turn survives a failure write). Suite 1444 green, tsc clean.

Fixed the team-not-playing guard being bypassed when the query also names a league. getScores keyed the guard on ref.viaTeam, which is only set when the league resolved VIA the team map; 'did the Lakers win, NBA scores?' resolves via the LEAGUES word (viaTeam unset) but still names a team, so it dumped the whole slate. Now keyed on a new namesKnownTeam(query) (any TEAM_LEAGUE regex hit, independent of league resolution) -> teamNotPlaying fires whenever a named team has no game today. 1 new test. Suite 1445 green, tsc clean.

Added the isCancelled() guard to the reminderOnly fire path. The main/alert-silent/digest-null paths all check isCancelled() before their side effects (timeout late-finish guard), but reminderOnly awaited deps.send + completed with no check — so a send stalling past the 90s fire timeout could double-send the most common reminder type ('take my meds') when the retry tick ran. Now guards before send+complete like the others. 1 new test (stalled reminderOnly send doesn't double-deliver). Suite 1446 green, tsc clean.

Fixed chart/trend series poisoned by a stray number in a non-degraded error reply. recordPoint recorded any extractable number, so 'the price page returned a 404 error' stored 404 -> a phantom spike in the watch's series. New looksLikeErrorReply (alerts.ts) flags soft-failure shapes (error/failed/couldn't/no data/timed out/blocked + status codes ONLY inside an explicit error phrase, so a real $450/Nasdaq 5900 isn't flagged); recordPoint now skips those. 5 new tests (looksLikeErrorReply true/false cases + recordPoint skips 404-reply but records a $450 price). Suite 1448 green, tsc clean.

Added a translate tool: new src/lib/translate.ts (parseTranslateRequest + buildTranslatePrompt + translate) wrapping the in-loop LLM — 'translate X to Spanish' / 'how do you say X in Japanese' / 'read me this page in English: <url>'. Added convert_units: new src/lib/units-convert.ts — a DETERMINISTIC converter over fixed factor tables (temperature affine; length/mass/volume+cooking by factor) with parseUnitConvert (incl. no-space temp '180C to F', compound '5 ft 11 in' summed, 'of <thing>' ignored), convertUnit (null on unknown/cross-dimension), formatConvert, runConvert. Added meal_ideas tool: new src/lib/meals.ts over keyless TheMealDB (filter-by-ingredient, search-by-name for a full recipe, random). parseMealRequest routes 'what can I make with chicken and rice' (first ingredient), 'recipe for X'/'how do I make X' (full recipe), and 'dinner ideas'/'random meal' (random full recipe); returns idea lists or a full recipe (ingredients+measures+steps+source). Added get_suntimes: new src/lib/suntimes.ts over Open-Meteo daily sunrise/sunset/daylight (tz=auto, local ISO), reusing weather's geocode+pickCandidate. isSunRequest/sunDayIndex/sunPlace/parseSunTimes/formatSunTimes/getSunTimes. 'what time is sunset today'/'sunrise tomorrow in Denver'/'how much daylight' now exact instead of degrading to weather/web_search. 18 new tests, suite 1498 green, tsc clean. call-tested:true (Open-Meteo daily sun endpoint live 200 via ctx_execute).

Fixed translate grabbing the first in/to as the target. Was: / (to|in|into)s+(lang)/ matched the FIRST preposition + lazily ran to EOS, so 'I want to go to the beach to Spanish' -> target 'go to the beach to Spanish', a bogus language surfaced as an authoritative translation. Now the target is the FINAL 'to/into/in <lang>' clause anchored to end-of-string (1-2 letter-only words), and only that matched clause is stripped from the body. URL captured before the target scan so 'translate <url> to French' still works. 2 new regression tests. Suite 1499 green, tsc clean.

Fixed get_suntimes wrongly refusing a located user. The dispatch used a broad / ins+[A-Za-z]/ to decide 'named place', which fired on 'in the evening'/'in winter' -> it dropped the saved coords (passed only near) but sunPlace then rejected those tails -> no place + no coords -> 'which city?' for a user whose location IS stored. Now decides via sunPlace(request) (the same extractor getSunTimes uses): a real place passes coords as near, no place uses coords directly. 1 new regression test. Suite 1500 green, tsc clean.

Fixed 'cup to oz' failing as cross-type. Bare 'oz'/'ounce' maps to MASS, so the canonical kitchen conversion (1 cup = 8 fl oz) hit the dim-mismatch reject. convertUnit now reinterprets a bare oz as FLUID ounce when exactly the other side is a volume unit; oz stays mass when both sides are mass (16 oz = 1 lb), and a genuine cross-dim (cup->kg, kg->miles) still returns null. 2 new/updated tests. Suite 1501 green, tsc clean.

Added 'open now' to near-me. New src/lib/openhours.ts — a lightweight OSM opening_hours evaluator (isOpenNow: weekday ranges/lists + time windows + split windows + 24/7 + explicit closed; unknown on an exotic rule, never a wrong open/closed) + openTag. formatPlaces takes an optional {dow,mins} local time: tags each place open-now/closed-now (instead of raw hours) + lists OPEN places first. find_nearby dispatch computes the user's local day+minute from deps.nowMs+tzOffsetMin. So 'pharmacy near me' at 9pm no longer leads with one that closed at 6. Back-compat: no clock -> raw hours as before. 18 new tests, suite 1511 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (pure offline eval + formatting).

Fixed two dead calc paths. (1) A bare '%' BETWEEN two operands ('17 % 5', '17 % (2+3)') is now modulo — the percent-idiom rewrite only fires when '%' TRAILS a number ('20% of', '50 - 20%'), so it no longer eats the operator form into a malformed expr. (2) toRpn now counts function arity (seed 1 at '(', +1 per comma at that depth) and evalRpn folds it: min/max are variadic ('max(1,2,3)'->3), and fixed-arity fns (sqrt/loanpayment/...) throw a friendly 'takes N arguments' instead of silent residue. Also: normalizeExpr now strips only true thousands-commas (digit,comma,exactly-3-digits) so arg-separator commas survive for arity counting. 5 new calc tests, suite 1513 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (pure offline evaluator).

Scheduled/recipe agent replies no longer lose their tail. The plain scheduled-agent + recipe path set body=formatReply(res.reply) (trimmed to 1200) and passed the trimmed text as BOTH full and sent to recordSend, so a long daily/recipe answer arrived cut off and 'more' wrongly said 'that's the whole answer' — the dropped tail was gone. (The digest path had already been fixed via fullText; this path hadn't.) Added an optional formatReplyParts dep (untrimmed + phone-sized views) wired in index.ts; the path now caches the UNTRIMMED body as fullText when it differs from what was sent, so 'more' pages the remainder — mirroring the digest fix. Back-compat: without formatReplyParts it falls back to trimmed-only. 2 new runner tests (long reply pages tail; short reply back-compat), suite 1515 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (offline runner test w/ mock agent + injected clock).

Quiet hours no longer defers an explicit wall-clock alarm past its time. The runner deferred EVERY non-alert schedule that landed in the quiet window to the window end — including a 'once' with clockTime ('wake me at 6am', 'remind me tomorrow 7:00'), so a 6am alarm inside a midnight-8am quiet window fired at 8am, defeating it. Now clock-time onces (kind==='once' && clockTime===true) are exempt from the quiet defer, mirroring the alert-check exemption; a RELATIVE once ('in 20 min', no clockTime flag) still defers since its instant is incidental, not chosen. 2 new runner tests (clock-once fires on time in quiet hours; relative once still defers), suite 1517 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (offline runner test, injected clock + quietUntil).

Added a keyless date_math tool. New src/lib/datecalc.ts: a pure deterministic calendar evaluator (today injected, no Date.now inside, UTC-midnight day math so no DST drift). Handles 'how many days until <date/holiday>' (rolls a past bare date to next year), 'what day of the week is/was <date>', 'how old if born <date>' (years + months), 'days between X and Y', and 'date in N days/weeks'. Parses ISO / US-numeric / month-name / today-tomorrow-yesterday, plus common US holidays by name (Christmas, Thanksgiving computed as 4th-Thu-Nov, Halloween, July 4th, New Year's, Valentine's...). Wired: TOOLS[] entry + dispatch (computes user's LOCAL today from nowMs+tzOffsetMin) + prompt menu line + HELP + sorted tool-list test + a dispatch routing test. 17 new tests, suite 1533 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (pure offline eval + dispatch test). Previously these fell to a slow browse or a hallucinated guess since calc is arithmetic-only.

Added acknowledged/escalating reminders — the daily-habit hook (meds/water/standup). 'keep reminding me to take my meds every 15 min' / 'nag me to stretch every 20 min' / 'remind me to X every 30 min until I say done' now create a sticky reminder: an interval + reminderOnly + sticky flag. It re-pings on the interval, each fire appends '(reply "done" when you've handled it and I'll stop)'; a bare 'done'/'stop'/'ok'/'got it'/✅ reply removes it (isStickyAck + acknowledgeSticky, scoped to sticky only so a normal 'done' can't wipe real schedules and only fires when hasSticky). Self-caps after DEFAULT_STICKY_MAX (8, env RELAY_STICKY_MAX_FIRES) fires in complete() so a forgotten nag can't ping forever. Requires an explicit re-ping cue (keep/nag/until-done) so a plain 'every 15 min' stays a normal interval. Wired: schedule.ts (fields+parse+complete cap+ack/hasSticky methods), runner echo hint, handler ack-catch (before snooze), index stickyAck dep + sticky confirm wording + scheduleCue, HELP + .env.example. 10 new tests, suite 1543 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (offline parse/store/handler tests).

Fixed 2 regressions the audit found in the just-shipped sticky reminders. (1) SCOPE: a 'done' reply wiped EVERY sticky reminder, so acking the meds nag silently deleted an unrelated 'drink water every 30m' too. Now the runner stamps lastFiredMs on each confirmed sticky ping (markStickyFired) and acknowledgeSticky removes only the MOST-RECENTLY-FIRED one (falls back to all only if several exist and none has fired yet). (2) BUDGET: a transient send/anvil outage counted each failed fire toward the anti-nag cap via complete(), so a brief Telegram outage could exhaust stickyMax and self-delete a 'nag me until done' the user never saw ping. complete() now takes a `fired` flag; the runner's failure path passes fired:false so a failed send advances the interval to retry WITHOUT burning budget — only a confirmed send counts (mirrors the once transient-retry contract). 4 new tests (2 store scope/budget + 2 runner fired-stamp/fail-no-burn), suite 1547 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (offline store + runner tests).

Weather now answers time-of-day rain questions with WHEN, not a whole-day max. Added &hourly=precipitation_probability,temperature_2m to the existing keyless Open-Meteo call; parseForecast now builds an hours[] array (local date+hour+precip+temp from timezone=auto). New resolveHourWindow maps named dayparts (morning/afternoon/evening/tonight/noon), a specific 'at 3pm'/'at 15:00', and 'later today'/'rest of the day' (anchored to the location's current local hour) to an hour window; formatWeatherHourly slices those hours and summarizes rain likelihood + the peak-rain hour + temp range ('Austin afternoon: likely rain (up to 80%, around 3pm), 72-75F'). Dispatch resolves most-specific-first: hourly window -> future day -> current; nowHour from nowMs+tzOffsetMin. Tool `when` + prompt updated to route 'this afternoon'/'tonight'/'at 3pm'. 8 new tests; live-probed the Open-Meteo hourly URL (200, local timestamps, 168h) so call-tested:true for the data source (agent wiring offline-tested).

Fixed feedItemKey truncating to 120 chars, which collided distinct long titles. Two different feed entries (verbose news/marketplace/job titles) sharing a 120-char prefix got the same dedup key, so the second was treated as already-seen + a genuinely-new item silently never pinged (read as 'nothing new'). feedItemKey now appends a short FNV-1a hash of the FULL normalized text when it exceeds 120 chars, so distinct long titles get distinct keys; a short title is unchanged (no hash) so existing phrasing-drift stability holds; a genuine repeat still keys identically. Both feed paths (alert-runner id-or-title key + the checkAlert list path) use feedItemKey so both are covered. 1 new test, suite 1583 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (pure key fn).

Error-shaped agent replies no longer false-fire alerts or poison the baseline. looksLikeErrorReply was only used to skip the time-series point, NOT the trigger decision — so a soft failure like 'the page returned a 404' yielded extractValue()=404, satisfied a 'below 50000' predicate/threshold, pinged a FALSE alarm showing an error string, and on a threshold poisoned the baseline so the next check re-fired. Added a single guard right after value is computed (mirrors the degraded guard): looksLikeErrorReply(value) -> hold, keep last-good baseline, stay silent — covering condition/threshold/change/feed/series paths at once. Also guarded the watchlist member loop so an error-shaped member holds its baseline. 2 new tests (error-shaped reply holds baseline + doesn't fire; first-run seed test switched to a non-error numberless value), suite 1584 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (offline runner tests).

Digest no longer shows a soft-error reply as real briefing content. digest-runner only demoted a member to '(couldn't fetch)' on a thrown error or the degraded flag; a non-degraded reply whose TEXT is a fetch failure ('btc: the page returned a 404') became a 'real' section verbatim + miscounted toward real content so the honest all-failed notice never fired. Now the agent body AND the chain output are gated with looksLikeErrorReply (same guard the alert path uses) -> demoted to '(couldn't fetch)' + status 'failed'. So an error member shows the fallback line, and an all-error digest emits the 'couldn't build it this time' note instead of a briefing of error strings. 2 new tests (one error member demoted; all-error -> all-failed note), suite 1586 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (offline runner tests).

Added monthly + yearly recurring reminders — the two universal recurring errands the once/daily/weekly/interval set couldn't express (bills, birthdays). New ScheduleKind 'monthly'/'yearly' + dayOfMonth/month fields. Parse: 'pay rent on the 1st of every month' / 'every month on the 15th' -> monthly; 'mom's birthday every year on June 3' / 'every year on 12/25' / month-day / D-of-Month / M/D forms -> yearly. Detected BEFORE interval (whose regex needs 'every N unit'). Reuses the existing keyless date helpers: domAtMs (next future day-of-month, skips short months) for monthly, dateAtMs (this-year-or-next month+day) for yearly. complete() reschedules both; restampTz re-stamps both on a later /setlocation; add() persists the fields; isClockTime (tz-warn + first-reminder-tz-ask) + the schedule cue + the confirm verb + HELP all cover the new kinds. A plain 'on the 1st' with no monthly cue still stays a one-shot. 7 new tests (5 parse + 2 complete-reschedule), suite 1593 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (offline parse/store tests, fixed clock).

alertEdit now hedges a failed disk write like every other write path. 'change btc to below 45000' confirmed 'Updated' unconditionally, so a failed persist silently reverted the trigger to the old threshold on restart — user watched the wrong number with no warning. index.alertEdit now returns saved (alerts.lastSaveOk(), which updateTrigger already sets) + the handler appends 'I couldn't save that to disk — it may revert if I restart' when saved===false, matching alertDefine/scheduleAdd/etc. 1 new handler test, suite 1594 green, tsc clean. call-tested:false (offline handler test).
